comments.body:
Carried from the Gerrit `LLM-Review` bot on change 3211 patchset 2 (advisory, non-blocking), because this ticket consumes the number the finding is about.

`tests/integration/test_similar_tickets_scale.py:240`, in `test_the_cold_catch_up_cost_at_that_scale_is_emitted_as_a_number`, ends with:

```python
assert isinstance(p95, float)
assert p95 > 0.0
```

Any wall-clock sample satisfies both unconditionally. The test cannot fail for any behavior of the code under test, so it is a measurement emitter wearing a test's name, not a regression oracle.

That matters here because this ticket records "the measured cold-catch-up p95" in ADR 0122. The number that test prints is the number this ADR will cite, and nothing currently checks it against anything.

Two separable things to settle when this ticket is worked:

1. Which p95 the ADR cites, and on what hardware. A wall-clock figure measured on one host is not portable; 47c8 already had to replace a wall-clock budget with a counted invariant plus a same-host ratio after `macos-latest` measured 545 ms against a 500 ms budget where the same code measured 107 ms locally. The ADR should say what was measured, on what, rather than present a bare millisecond figure as a property of the code.
2. Whether that test keeps a name that claims it tests something. Either it gains an assertion that can fail, or it is renamed and documented as a measurement harness.

No change was made to the test under 47c8: the finding is advisory and 47c8 is the keystone blocking this ticket, 80a5 and 2041, so resetting its gates for a non-blocking test-naming issue was not worth the round trip.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

ADR 0122 is the binding design record for similar-ticket retrieval. Three of its statements are wrong once the sibling stories land, and one requirement of the parent epic is unmet by the ADR as written.

## Approach

### The tiering decision is absent

ADR 0122 compared candidates and adopted `vector`, but it records no decision about what runs when no model provider is configured. The architecture the sibling stories build is two-tiered: a lexical FTS5 default available in every installation, and an opt-in embedding upgrade over the same index. An ADR that does not record that split leaves the default undocumented and leaves a future reader unable to tell whether the lexical path is a fallback, a deliberate tier, or dead code.

### The deployment precondition is too broad

The "Deployment precondition" section (`docs/adr/0122-similar-ticket-retrieval.md:180-201`) ends at `:198` with the claim that adoption "depends on that grant being applied before the index can be built anywhere but a developer's own credentials". That was true when the only candidate was embedding-backed. It is false for the lexical tier, which needs no credentials at all. Left as written, it tells operators the feature is unavailable to them when it is not.

The precondition is narrowed so it constrains the embedding tier rather than the index as a whole.

### The ADR reads as single-provider, but the implementation is not

The ADR names Titan v2 and Haiku 4.5 throughout — in its title, its per-ticket cost table at `:170-171`, and its precondition at `:184`. Read as a design record, that makes a specific Bedrock model pair a property of the architecture. The sibling embedding story lands `infer_embedding_model` dispatch across more than one provider, so the ADR as written contradicts the code it governs and would tell a future reader that rebar's retrieval is Bedrock-only.

rebar must run against a wide variety of providers and models. The embedding tier is therefore recorded as provider-agnostic, with the Bedrock pair identified as the configuration that was measured rather than the one that is required.

### No latency figure is recorded, and a bare one would not be portable

ADR 0122 reports recall, significance and cost, but no latency figure anywhere. The parent epic requires the ADR to report the cold-catch-up p95.

A bare millisecond figure presented as a property of the code is not portable and does not survive contact with another host. The sibling index story demonstrated this directly: a 500 ms wall-clock budget that measured 107 ms on the development host measured 545 ms on `macos-latest`, and the criterion had to be replaced with a counted invariant plus a same-host ratio. The ADR records each measurement together with the conditions that produced it, so a reader can tell what would have to be re-measured on their own hardware.

The figures the sibling story emitted, on a 10,000-ticket store on the development host: cold catch-up p95 12,455 ms over 5 runs; cold full rebuild 16,940 ms; warm query p95 120.8 ms over 25 runs, hashing zero ticket directories in the steady state.

### What this task does not touch

The ARN sentence at `:184-189` was already amended by the sibling IAM task, which has merged. This task leaves it alone.

### Scope

Documentation only. No source change, no configuration change, no new mechanism. The vacuous assertion in `tests/integration/test_similar_tickets_scale.py:240` that emits the cited p95 is a test-quality defect outside this task's docs-only scope; it is tracked as `average-random-piranha`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `docs/adr/0122-similar-ticket-retrieval.md` names the lexical tier as the default that requires no model provider. Checked by: reading the ADR.
- [x] The ADR names the embedding tier as opt-in. Checked by: reading the ADR.
- [x] The ADR's deployment precondition constrains the embedding tier rather than the index as a whole. Checked by: the ADR no longer asserting the index requires a developer's own credentials.
- [x] The ADR identifies the embedding tier as provider-agnostic, naming the measured Bedrock model pair as the configuration benchmarked rather than the one required. Checked by: reading the ADR.
- [x] The ADR reports the cold-catch-up p95 as a numeric figure taken from the sibling index story's measurement. Checked by: reading the figure.
- [x] Each latency figure the ADR reports is stated together with the store size, the host it was measured on, and the sample count. Checked by: reading each figure.
- [x] No file outside `docs/` is modified. Checked by: the change's diff.
